real_qa.q: How much capital was invested in the space economy in 2025 and Q4?
real_qa.r: 2025 set an all-time record with $55 billion invested. Q4 saw $17 billion invested through 135 different rounds, despite the U.S. government shutdown that lasted half the quarter and grounded aviation.

real_qa.q: What is the SpaceX IPO significance for the space economy in 2026?
real_qa.r: SpaceX IPO represents a Netscape moment for deep tech and space economy. With 10 million plus Starlink subscribers, a direct-to-cell roadmap, and orbital data center narrative tapping into AI, this IPO could make SpaceX one of the top 10 most valuable companies in the world and reprice the entire market, attracting institutional capital and encouraging other companies to list.

real_qa.q: Why is orbital data center infrastructure dependent on Starship launch economics?
real_qa.r: Orbital data centers do not work on the current Falcon 9 launch paradigm because launch costs need to come down significantly. Starship coming operational is key to making orbital data centers economically viable, allowing SpaceX to launch this type of infrastructure at lower costs.

real_qa.q: What is Golden Dome and how does it impact space defense investment?
real_qa.r: Golden Dome doubled the space defense market at least for the foreseeable future. real_qa.q: Which geospatial intelligence companies are receiving investment for world models integration?

real_qa.r: Infrastructure saw 50 acquisitions in 2025 with an exit value of $1.3 billion, setting a new record for acquisition count. This marks a recovery from previous years where acquisition count skyrocketed but values stayed low, now showing acquirers are paying premiums again.
